headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: xonsh can write/egress by default while godot_rl_agents has no documented isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and xonsh, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, xonsh can read/write files and run shell commands, so if the pair is manually bridged through files or stdin/stdout, attacker-controlled content could be interpreted as instructions. godot_rl_agents shows no such bridge itself.
conditions: IF the operator copies xonsh output into a file that godot_rl_agents later consumes as instructions
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable manual copy-paste between agent outputs and agent inputs
Prefix all exchanged text with a non-executable delimiter
Review any file-based handoff before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh has broad network egress and filesystem access, while godot_rl_agents is documented only as a game-playing repo with no explicit data-handling controls. If they share files or environment state, xonsh can exfiltrate whatever godot_rl_agents produces. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default local workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree
IF godot_rl_agents outputs sensitive artifacts into files that xonsh can read
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Mount the game agent workspace read-only for xonsh
Block xonsh network egress during shared runs
Scan outputs for secrets before any xonsh processing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and has no multiple-instance support; godot_rl_agents has no documented concurrency or locking. If both touch the same directory, write conflicts are plausible even though modify_git_state is false. Uncertainty about the game agent's runtime surfaces pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF xonsh launches concurrent subprocesses against shared files
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Run xonsh with write access removed for shared paths
Avoid concurrent instances of xonsh on the same workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: xonsh can act on shell output and filesystem contents, so if it consumes artifacts from godot_rl_agents without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect commands or file changes. godot_rl_agents has no documented validation layer or downstream checks. The pathway exists, but there is no evidence of irreversible automated action, so medium fits.
conditions: IF xonsh treats godot_rl_agents output as authoritative input
IF xonsh uses that output to generate shell commands or file edits
mitigations: Add a human review step before xonsh acts on outputs
Require schema validation on exchanged artifacts
Log and diff proposed commands before execution
Limit xonsh to read-only analysis for the first pass

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, and xonsh is open-source with no handled secrets listed. The only concrete compliance concern is that xonsh can process filesystem contents and environment variables, so a local policy mismatch could arise if sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace. The other agent is not cited for a separate compliance regime.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in files or environment variables that xonsh reads
IF local retention rules require deletion that xonsh workflows do not enforce
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use synthetic or redacted inputs
Set a short-lived temp directory for runs
Document deletion steps after each session
